objects.name: bowtie
objects.description: One way an enterprise could lose control of something through its AI systems, drawn as a bow-tie. Data leaking out through a prompt, a retrieval index or an agent is the worked example.

indexes.name: category
indexes.description: The register browse by category, which is a grouping this domain draws and the module does not.

objects.name: pathway
objects.description: One route by which sensitive information escapes through an AI system, or one route by which the harm of that escape unfolds: a prompt pasted into an unapproved service, a document retrieved for the wrong user, a regulator told too late.

objects.name: control
objects.description: One safeguard the enterprise runs around its AI systems: an approved gateway, input filtering, permission-aware retrieval, a kill switch, an incident procedure.

objects.name: barrier
objects.description: One safeguard claimed to stand on one route, such as input filtering on the prompt route and not yet on the agent tool-call route.

objects.name: evidence
objects.description: One red-team result, log review, configuration export or audit finding about one barrier.

objects.name: assessment
objects.description: One rating of how likely and how damaging a loss of control is judged to be, before and after the safeguards as they actually are.

objects.name: remediation
objects.description: One piece of work to close a gap in the AI safeguards, with an owner and a date.

objects.name: ai_system
objects.description: One AI application, model or agent the enterprise runs. The AI safety register's own object: this module has no rule that touches it, and declares no role it could fill.

fields.name: name
fields.description: What the system is called inside the enterprise.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: What sort of system it is, in the enterprise's own words: a public chatbot, an internal copilot, a retrieval assistant, an autonomous agent.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: Who is accountable for the system, as the mount's own reference to a person or a team.

fields.name: doc
fields.description: Everything else the enterprise records about the system: its provider, the data classes it may see, the tools it may call.

indexes.name: owner
indexes.description: Finds the systems one owner answers for.
